title: Kubernetes Graceful-Shutdown Plan
description: A structured plan for a pod's shutdown lifecycle — preStop sleep, grace-period budget, signal handling, readiness behavior — so this skill's timing rules and Quality Gates can be checked deterministically by scripts/kubernetes_graceful_shutdown_audit.mjs.

preStopSleepSeconds.description: Duration of the preStop sleep hook (0 = no hook). Covers the EndpointSlice/kube-proxy/LB convergence race: 5s small cluster, 10-15s typical cloud LB, 30s+ large clusters.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: The pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds (Kubernetes default 30). Shared between preStop and the post-SIGTERM drain.

drainBudgetSeconds.description: Worst-case time the app needs after SIGTERM to finish in-flight work. preStop + drain must fit inside the grace period with margin.

sigtermHandlerRegistered.description: True if the app registers a SIGTERM handler that drains (server.close() / srv.Shutdown(ctx)) rather than ignoring the signal.

immediateExitOnSigterm.description: True if the handler calls process.exit()/os.Exit() without draining — the connection-reset anti-pattern.

pid1IsApp.description: True if the runtime itself is PID 1 (exec-form CMD, or tini init) so SIGTERM is not swallowed by a shell wrapper.

hardDeadlineShorterThanGrace.description: True if the drain has an in-app hard ceiling (setTimeout + closeAllConnections / context.WithTimeout) shorter than the grace period.

readinessFlipsOnShutdown.description: True if the readiness probe returns 503 once shutdown begins — complementing the preStop sleep.

readinessFlipReplacesSleep.description: True if the design relies on the readiness flip INSTEAD of a preStop sleep. The flip only helps the next propagation cycle; this fails the audit.

backgroundWorkersHandleShutdown.description: True if queue consumers, cron loops, and DB pools are cancelled by the same shutdown context as the HTTP server.
